title: Garbage-Collector Dependent Connection Management
pattern: Relying on object garbage collection or finalization to close high-value system resources like database connections or sockets.
why_bad: Garbage collection is non-deterministic. Unreferenced connections can sit open in memory for minutes or hours before the collector reclaims them, exhausting the server's connection pool or file descriptors.
detection: Instantiating closeable resources (files, sockets, database connections) without explicit closure calls or placement within scoped resource management constructs.
counterexample: In-memory objects that have no backing external system resources and rely safely on automated garbage collection.
fix: Bind connection lifecycle to explicit scopes using `try-with-resources` blocks (or standard Rust scoping and deterministic destructors).
source: Martin Fowler, *Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture* / passage [655, 656].
